summary: Clarifies the status of RFCs and gives guidance to future RFC authors. In a sense it is a specification for RFCs themselves. Replaced by RFC 1111 and RFC 1543 and RFC 2223.

plainLanguage.summary: RFC 825 tells authors to state what an RFC is for and sets basic rules for its file format. Later RFCs replaced this guidance.

subtitle: A guide to identifying an RFC's purpose and formatting it for distribution.

tldr.problem: Readers need to know whether an RFC specifies a protocol, starts a discussion, shares information, gives status, or reports a meeting; files also need to work on varied equipment.
tldr.mechanism: RFC 825 asks authors to state an RFC's intention near the beginning and sets ASCII, page-height, line-width, and formatting rules.
tldr.outcome: The memo itself is a specification for RFCs and was later obsoleted by RFCs 1111, 1543, and 2223.

today: RFC 825 was obsoleted by RFCs 1111, 1543, and 2223. It is an earlier guide to RFC purpose statements and formatting.

sections.title: Why State an RFC's Intention
sections.content: RFC 825 says that RFCs may make information available, start or continue discussion, or specify a protocol. It asks every RFC to include a statement of intention on the title page or in one of the first paragraphs.
sections.plainLanguage: Readers should be able to tell what kind of document they are reading. RFC 825 asks authors to say so near the beginning.

sections.title: Five Kinds of Intention
sections.content: The memo provides example paragraphs for a Specification, Discussion, Information, Status, and Report. It says the samples need not be copied word for word, but the general intent of the RFC must be clear.
sections.plainLanguage: The examples distinguish a proposed standard from discussion, information, a status update, or a meeting report. Authors may use different wording if the purpose remains clear.

sections.title: Formatting Rules
sections.content: The memo sets ASCII as the character code. Each page is limited to 58 lines followed by a form feed on a line by itself, and each line is limited to 72 characters followed by carriage return and line feed. It disallows overstriking and underlining, including in headers and footers.
sections.plainLanguage: The format limits page height and line width so files can be printed or displayed on varied equipment. It also disallows overstriking and underlining.

sections.title: Distribution and Submission
sections.content: RFCs are stored as public-access files, and a short message is sent to the distribution list when a memo becomes available. RFC 825 lists one address for requests to join or leave the list and another for RFC submissions.
sections.plainLanguage: New memos are stored as public files, and the distribution list is notified. The memo gives separate contact addresses for list changes and submissions.
